scope: Massless helicity +1/-1 induced representation and wedge modular localization on the same canonical H1
conventions: Metric eta=diag(1,-1,-1,-1); translation phase exp(i eta(a,p)); Bx(t) uses positive sinh off diagonal.
Proper orthochronous Lorentz group SO+(1,3), extended to the proper group by antiunitary spacetime inversion. Integer helicities +1/-1 descend to this group.
rho=sqrt(q2^2+q3^2)>0; p=(rho cosh r,rho sinh r,q2,q3); k*=(1,0,0,1).
Rx(phi)e3=(0,-sin(phi),cos(phi)) with cos(phi)=q3/rho, sin(phi)=-q2/rho. Define the rotation matrix directly from these coordinates, avoiding a branch-dependent angle.
zeta is the unit-complex character of the SO(2) rotational quotient of ISO(2); its two translations act trivially. It is not a character of a full O(2) stabilizer.

checks.calculation: Bz(log rho)k*=rho k*. Rx(phi) sends rho e3 to (0,q2,q3). Bx(r) yields exactly p. Therefore s(p)k*=p.
checks.null_set_clarification: At q=0, rho/r are unavailable. Either define operators a.e. with an explicit null-set convention, or complete s on p=(E,+/-E,0,0) by Ry(+/-pi/2)Bz(log E). The cone vertex has zero measure and is excluded from the positive mass shell.

checks.calculation: c(L,p) fixes k*, because s(L^-1 p)k*=L^-1 p. Inserting s(L1^-1 p)s(L1^-1 p)^-1 proves c(L1 L2,p)=c(L1,p)c(L2,L1^-1 p). D=diag(zeta,conj zeta) is a unitary representation of that stabilizer; D(c) therefore obeys the same law.

Canonical shell coordinates have measure dq2 dq3 dp1/E. The change p1=rho sinh r has dp1=E dr, hence the rapidity measure is dq2 dq3 dr. Under an axial boost the spatial Jacobian is Eprime/E; rotations have Jacobian 1. Rotations and boosts generate SO+(1,3), establishing invariance of dp/E. The factor 2 relative to dp/(2E) is an invariant constant.

Unitarity follows from D(c) unitary and invariant measure. The cocycle plus eta(b,L^-1p)=eta(Lb,p) gives U(a,L)U(b,M)=U(a+Lb,LM). Positive-energy spectrum is the future null shell. Strong continuity follows first on continuous compactly supported vectors away from q=0 using the continuous rotation matrix and dominated convergence, then on all H1 by density and unitarity; no globally smooth angular branch is needed.
checks.canonical_match: Fib=EuclideanSpace complex (Fin 2), H1=Lp Fib 2 orbitalMeasure(0), and orbitPairing is precisely (+---). Thus the translation subgroup is the existing U1, not a new scalar product or measure.

checks.calculation: s(Bx(t)p)=Bx(t)s(p) because q and rho stay fixed and r changes to r+t. Hence c(Bx(t),p)=I and U(0,Bx(t))f(q,r)=f(q,r-t), exactly the convention of B0 and productRapidityShift.

Rx(pi) commutes with Bx(r) and sends q to -q, preserving rho. Rx(phi(-q))=Rx(phi(q)-pi) as an SO(2) matrix. Thus c(Rx(pi),p)=I a.e. and U(Rx(pi)) pulls back q to -q. If working on the double cover, central 2pi factors may occur in a lifted section but act trivially for helicities +/-1.

Let P swap the two components. Theta=P complex_conjugation. P conj(D(c)) P=D(c); hence Theta commutes with the Lorentz subgroup. It conjugates exp(i eta(a,p)) to exp(-i eta(a,p)), so Theta U(a) Theta=U(-a), and Theta^2=I. The helicity pair is essential: a single nonzero-helicity summand cannot use this same involution.

Write R=Rx(pi)=diag(1,1,-1,-1). J=U(R)Theta acts as swap(conj f(p0,p1,-q)), is antiunitary, and J^2=U(R^2)=I. J U(a,L) J=U(-Ra,RLR)=U(jW a,jW L jW), with jW=-R=diag(-1,-1,1,1). In particular, edge translations are preserved rather than inverted, explaining why omitting q reflection is geometrically wrong.

Delta^(it)=B0(-2pi t) matches BGL right-wedge convention. J commutes with this unitary group but is antiunitary, so J(log Delta)J=-log Delta and J Delta J=Delta^-1. The spectral calculus defines positive nonsingular Delta with dense-domain Delta^(1/2), and S=J Delta^(1/2) is a closed dense antilinear involution. K=Fix(S) is standard. Covariance fixes K(gW) independently of the representative g; positive energy then gives isotony and wedge duality gives locality.
checks.formalization_boundary: These BGL applications are cited mathematical results and this review is a written derivation. They are not newly compiled Lean terms for the 4D representation or net.

checks.calculation: The chosen real swap fixes a convention. Replacing J by exp(i chi)J preserves involutivity and covariance but replaces K by exp(i chi/2)K. It is a unitarily equivalent net, not equality of the original subspace. For this single +/-1 pair an involutive swapping antiunitary requires the same off-diagonal phase on both components. BGL irreducible uniqueness wording must not be applied verbatim to the reducible doublet.

critical_warning: Do not infer geometrical localization merely from J^2=I and J Delta J=Delta^-1. The full relation J U(a,L) J=U(jW a,jW L jW), the positive-energy representation, and its match to the canonical B0 are the indispensable bridges.
